description: Major expedition source decisions. Mapped means the identified major phase has dated anchors, not that every daily position is known. Partial, held and disputed entries preserve the remaining precise questions.

entries.name: Cabot’s Matthew
entries.note: The only uncontested, place-specific day anchor in the inventory is the Bristol return. Toby gives May 2, Pasqualigo mid-May and John Day late May for departure. June 24 is associated with the landfall but the site remains unidentified.

anchors.name: Bristol departure
anchors.note: Sources place the departure in May but disagree on the day.

anchors.name: Eastern North American coast, unidentified landfall
anchors.note: Cape Breton, Newfoundland and additional sites have been proposed. No single point represents the landfall.

anchors.name: Bristol return
anchors.note: Contemporary chronology as reported by Newfoundland and Labrador Heritage.

remainingQuestions: Bristol departure day
Eastern North American landfall and homeward departure site

entries.name: Cabot’s subsequent fleet
entries.note: The Bristol departure is documented at month scale and the dated July dispatch reports an earlier, unlocated Irish diversion. Subsequent routes and any return remain unresolved.
remainingQuestions: Departure day
Date and identity of the Irish port
Voyage outcome for individual ships

entries.name: Roberval and France-Roi
entries.note: The outward fleet has exact port dates. France-Roy and repatriation have separately displayed activity evidence.

anchors.name: Newfoundland departure
anchors.note: Newfoundland departure in the museum history.

anchors.name: Cap-Rouge arrival
anchors.note: Reported in the latter part of July.

remainingQuestions: Day of arrival at Cap-Rouge
Dates of the inland exploration and arrival back in France
The primary account gives only approximate late-June departure from Newfoundland, despite 30 June in the museum chronology.

entries.name: Cook’s third voyage · Clerke and Gore return
entries.note: Two command phases now cover the renewed Arctic attempt and homeward voyage. Historical ship fixes distinguish the 18 July noon observation from the farther-north approach on 19 July.
remainingQuestions: Minor island calls, daily tacks, and narrow-channel passages are not a continuous recovered track.

entries.name: Columbus’s third voyage · Paria and Hispaniola
entries.note: Three dated Paria observations are added, with uncertainty over the landing locality and Columbus’s presence ashore. Hispaniola remains period-level context.
remainingQuestions: Published chronologies conflict on the August 1498 Hispaniola arrival day.
Inland movements, detention and the precise 1500 embarkation date require separate primary-source reconciliation.

entries.name: Columbus’s fourth voyage · Jamaica and return
entries.note: Jamaica arrival, rescue departure and Sanlúcar return are mapped from Porras and Navarrete. The eclipse retains its distinct record.
remainingQuestions: The sources distinguish Puerto Bueno arrival from beaching at Santa Gloria; no unsupported exact beginning of a continuous Santa Gloria stay is asserted.
Hispaniola rescue arrangements and Diego Méndez’s separate canoe voyage remain to be mapped.

entries.name: Franklin expedition · Beechey Island winter and Inuit accounts
entries.note: Contemporary grave inscriptions anchor the Beechey winter interval from January 1 through April 3. Greenland and an independent Baffin Bay sighting establish the approach. The first season’s true year follows the archaeological and grave evidence.
remainingQuestions: Day of ship arrival and departure at Beechey Island
Exact course between Baffin Bay, Wellington Channel and the winter camp

entries.name: Franklin expedition · ship abandonment
entries.note: The Victory Point note gives April 22 and a relative site about five leagues north-northwest of the cairn. The April 25 waypoint marks the shore record. Inuit testimony and archaeology contribute to accounts of later movements, while the exact 1848 abandonment positions remain unresolved.
remainingQuestions: Locations of both ships on April 22
Exact course and timing of separate survivors’ movements and any reboarding

entries.name: Robert McClure’s Investigator and rescue
entries.note: The ship, McClure’s 1852 search by sledge, Pim’s relief arrival, and evacuation and return have separate dated evidence. The records distinguish the ship’s multi-year icebound interval from over-ice travel by its crew.
remainingQuestions: Exact arrival day at Beechey after April 14, 1854
Additional dated coastal survey stations and the homeward vessel assignment of individual men

entries.name: Sverdrup’s second Fram expedition
entries.note: The dated ship itinerary represents all winter-base locations, the fourth winter and the return. Two separate sledge itineraries add the Ringnes and Beechey Island survey parties.
remainingQuestions: Additional day-and-place evidence for the Axel Heiberg and Devon Island parties
Exact mooring positions and complete movements near the winter bases

entries.name: Frederick Cook’s North Pole claim
entries.note: Documented Greenland departure and return movements now have their own itinerary. Cook’s April 21, 1908 polar claim remains disputed and has no polar position.
remainingQuestions: Actual route north of the Canadian Arctic islands and precise winter retreat movements
Upernavik arrival day differs by one day across sources

entries.name: Robert Peary and Matthew Henson expedition
entries.note: The Roosevelt, the Cape Columbia land anchoring and the sledge parties’ return are mapped separately. The North Pole location claimed for April 6, 1909 remains contested and has no route waypoint.
remainingQuestions: Precisely how far north the party traveled
Exact routes of individual support divisions across the ice

entries.name: Amundsen, Ellsworth and Nobile · Norge airship crossing
entries.note: Mapped in norge-transpolar-flight-1926 using air mode.

anchors.name: North Pole overflight
anchors.note: Airship passed over the North Pole.

remainingQuestions: Aerial line remains schematic between the documented stops.

entries.name: Byrd and Balchen · first South Pole overflight
entries.note: Mapped in byrd-south-pole-flight-1929 using air mode. Same-day return is described in the South Pole stop note.

anchors.name: Little America departure
anchors.note: The Floyd Bennett took off from Little America.

anchors.name: South Pole overflight
anchors.note: The aircraft flew over the Pole and returned to Little America.

remainingQuestions: The existing route represents the selected flight observations, not a complete aerial log.

entries.name: Amundsen and Sverdrup · Maud expedition
entries.note: The Northeast Passage and its wintering stops, detached sledging and mail parties, Bering–Seattle outfitting phase, Wisting and Sverdrup’s scientific drift and the Wainwright test flights now have distinct evidence. Drift positions are selected regional anchors.
remainingQuestions: Day-by-day drift positions and exact 1924–25 coastal mooring
Location and dates of individual Dahl–Wisting flights where published chronologies differ
Detailed sledge tracks in Chukotka

entries.name: Lincoln Ellsworth’s initial Antarctic flight expeditions
entries.note: The two Wyatt Earp staging voyages distinguish the aborted Ross Sea plan and Peninsula staging. The 3 January 1935 flight attempt and completed 1935 crossing lie beyond the timeline.

entries.name: Borchgrevink’s Ross Ice Shelf ski journey
entries.note: Cape Adare shore occupation and the Southern Cross survey have separate itineraries. The sledge party’s farthest south is an isolated observation with competing dates of 17 and 19 February.

entries.name: Bransfield, Smith and Palmer · early Antarctic Peninsula reports
entries.note: Smith’s disputed February sighting is a standalone observation, and his October landing and the later Bransfield–Smith naval survey have separate itineraries. Palmer’s 17 November report remains distinct and the interpretation of Hero’s log is disputed.
remainingQuestions: Compare the Hero log against Stackpole’s interpretation and identify any source-supported offshore observation positions for Palmer’s 1820–1821 survey.

entries.name: Biscoe, Kemp and Balleny · sealing-era Antarctic surveys
entries.note: Three separately documented ship itineraries distinguish log positions, Antarctic land reports and Freeman’s rock recovery.
remainingQuestions: Identify the site of Biscoe’s 21 February annexation from the original expedition material; use Balleny’s complete vessel log to date the return and Sabrina’s separation.
Compare Kemp’s reported coast position and the 26–27 December annotation with the original UK Hydrographic Office chart.

entries.name: Dumont d’Urville · Astrolabe and Zélée
entries.note: The Antarctic ship route is corrected to exclude the separate Dumoulin Islands landing party; its evidence identifier is preserved as an isolated point.
remainingQuestions: Pacific survey itinerary, first-voyage 1826–1829 work and separate local boat movements still need primary dated extraction.

entries.name: Southern Cross contemporaries and later national expeditions
entries.note: Valdivia, Gauss, Scotia, both Charcot expeditions, Shirase’s vessel and dash patrol, Filchner’s survey and drift, and Mawson’s deployment, sledging and relief seasons each have dated representations.
remainingQuestions: Extract Gauss’s field traverses, Charcot’s in-between survey fixes and Shirase’s shore sorties to Edward VII Land from the voyage journals.
Extract intermediate positions for Deutschland’s winter drift and the Morrell search sledge party, and other Australasian Antarctic Expedition sledge journeys and oceanographic cruises.

entries.name: Shackleton–Rowett expedition · Quest
entries.note: Wild’s survey, return to South Georgia, sub-Antarctic islands and final Atlantic return continue the earlier outward voyage and close at Plymouth.

entries.name: Mawson · BANZARE
entries.note: Discovery’s two field seasons have independent departure and return itineraries. The first season’s two documented air launches are standalone observations. Second-season air surveys have month-level context.
remainingQuestions: Extract individual 1931 flight takeoff, observations and landing fixes, and the late January 1930 air sorties near Proclamation Island, from the pilots’ logs and field charts.

entries.name: Aurora’s unplanned Ross Sea pack drift
entries.note: The deployment, Stenhouse’s drift with selected ship-log positions and return, and the stranded party remain independently mapped.

entries.name: Swedish Antarctic expedition · Antarctic shipwreck, Hope Bay and Paulet groups
entries.note: The Snow Hill stay, Antarctic sinking, Hope Bay and Paulet winter groups, Larsen reunion, and Argentine corvette rescue retain separate evidence. The corvette’s 8 November approach and Irízar’s overland arrival have distinct positions. The Paulet pickup day varies by source.
remainingQuestions: Extract dated South Georgia ship-survey anchors and Larsen’s intermediate boat positions between Paulet Island and Snow Hill.
Reconcile the 10 and 11 November dates for the Paulet pickup against the corvette’s log.

entries.name: Iberian Atlantic and Caribbean expeditions
entries.note: Dated anchor sets cover the documented Ojeda voyage, Pinzón’s return, the Solís expedition, and the 1513 Ponce de León circuit. Bastidas and the separate Vespucci attributions have individual activity entries. Cabral’s existing 1500 itinerary already represents the Brazilian phase.
remainingQuestions: Resolve the initial Atlantic landfalls and sailing days of Ojeda and Pinzón. The alleged 1497 Vespucci trip and the farthest southern positions of the documented Portuguese trip remain disputed.
Resolve the departure year and dated coastal anchorages of Bastidas and Juan de la Cosa. The 5 June 1500 authorization is distinct from the departure.
Compare the January and late-February Río de la Plata chronologies and the site of Solís’s death. Date the separate strandings and survivor returns.
Resolve the Florida landfall and Bimini detachment of 1513. The 1521 settlement and withdrawal have coarse coverage because the Florida landing site and day remain unsettled.
Corte-Real has separate research decisions in the Arctic and North Atlantic review.

entries.name: Spanish coastal expeditions and inland crossings
entries.note: Dated anchor sets cover Balboa’s Darién crossing, Hernández de Córdoba and Grijalva in the Gulf, Cortés’s coastal and overland advance, the Narváez fleet and separate survivor and return journeys, de Soto and Moscoso, and Coronado’s advance party. The deeper pass adds the separate Alarcón maritime force, explicit boat-party observations, and Alvarado/Padilla’s reconnaissance to Tiguex.
remainingQuestions: Trace the intermediate west Yucatán calls and Cuba returns for Córdoba and Grijalva. Compare the inconsistent Grijalva departure dates and the 8 and 10 June Tabasco chronology.
Resolve Narváez’s Apalachee and Aute camps, the Bay of Horses, and the separate boat paths. Determine individual route hypotheses for Cabeza de Vaca and his companions.
Resolve the exact sequence and places in de Soto’s late inland phases, including Mabila and the Mississippi crossings. Refine Moscoso’s winter site, split voyages and Gulf landings.

Coronado’s Plains camp and Quivira dates remain unresolved. Jaramillo gives the river crossing on Saints Peter and Paul (29 June), while later chronologies vary; no precise Arkansas crossing or Quivira arrival is fabricated. Alarcón’s upstream limit, Tovar and Cárdenas routes still need geographically defensible anchors.
Refine Cortés’s Cuba and Cozumel legs and the separate movements of the 1520 retreat and 1521 siege.

entries.name: Verrazzano, Basque whaling, Frobisher, Davis and Baffin
entries.note: Frobisher, Davis and Bylot–Baffin now have separate voyage itineraries. Basque whaling remains a recurring seasonal activity with archaeological evidence at Red Bay. Combine with the independently researched Verrazzano decision.
remainingQuestions: Detached ship courses, uncertain named sites and the ship-specific chronology of Basque whaling

entries.name: Marquette and Jolliet · Mississippi watershed
entries.note: The route has additional upper Fox and Mississippi day anchors, including the Quapaw turnaround. Separate month evidence covers the Fox–Wisconsin portage and Green Bay return.
remainingQuestions: Additional days on the Fox–Wisconsin and Illinois River routes
Exact Illinois and Quapaw village and landing sites

entries.name: Alexander Mackenzie and Indigenous guides
entries.note: Both expeditions now have separate outward, intermediate, portage and return evidence. The dated route uses the original journal for the return location in 1793.
remainingQuestions: Many precise campsite and nineteenth-century toponym identifications remain uncertain
Meandering river and trail segments between the listed anchors lack day-specific geometry

entries.name: Spanish Pacific Northwest survey voyages
entries.note: Dated tracks distinguish Pérez and Heceta in Santiago, Bodega and Mourelle in Sonora, Arteaga and Bodega’s partnered 1779 survey and separate returns, Martínez and Haro in 1788 and 1789, Eliza, Fidalgo, Quimper and Narváez/Carrasco in 1790–91, and the Galiano/Valdés, Fidalgo, Bodega and Caamaño expeditions of 1792.
remainingQuestions: Check day-by-day ship logs for unresolved sections and variant dates, particularly the 1774 July circuit, Heceta’s Monterey arrival, 1779 Bucareli and return dates, and separate arrival and return days of the 1788 and 1789 ships.

Map local pilot and survey-boat movements where evidence identifies the channels and stop dates. The 1789 Narváez departure and return are both documented at Nootka, and the entrance observation lacks a dated fix.
Locate additional dated offshore fixes where direct chords would cross islands and headlands. The existing Malaspina–Bustamante route has its own itinerary.

entries.name: La Pérouse voyage · Vanikoro wrecks
entries.note: Vanikoro now has a year-level map evidence point. Botany Bay anchoring is corrected from the offshore sighting on 24 January to 26 January.

anchors.name: Vanikoro wreck area
anchors.note: Regional wreck location. The day of loss is unknown.

remainingQuestions: The wreck day and route from Botany Bay to Vanikoro remain unknown.

entries.name: Malaspina and Bustamante · remaining survey phases
entries.note: The expanded baseline already covers selected Philippines, southwest Pacific and return stages; no unverified daily additions are made.

anchors.name: Nootka Sound
anchors.note: Arrival occurred on one of the two days.

remainingQuestions: Prioritize earlier South American port sequence, Atrevida’s separate Macao survey and scientific shore parties.
Retain Nootka arrival as disputed 12/13 August, never a two-day stay.

entries.name: Frobisher’s first voyage · Baffin Island phase
entries.note: The Gabriell’s August entrance and departure are now represented at bay scale, along with the documented October return. The first sighting’s island identification remains provisional.
remainingQuestions: Exact first North American sighting and position of the ship’s late-August anchorage

entries.name: Verrazzano’s coast survey after the New York Harbor entry
entries.note: A dated departure from Refugio, probably Narragansett Bay, extends the east-coast journey.
remainingQuestions: Refugio arrival remains 21/22 April; northern coastal observations lack securely extracted day/place pairs.

entries.note: The Cantino legend supports an ice-bound coast sighting in 1500. The sailing dates and an exact site cannot be established.
remainingQuestions: Departure and return chronology
Location and date of the sighting
entries.name: Gaspar Corte-Real’s first voyage

entries.note: The Lisbon chronology includes a later chronicler’s departure day and Pasqualigo’s exact-day report of a returning caravel. The American phases have only coast-level and year-level precision here.
remainingQuestions: Locations and dates of coastal stops
Date of the second caravel’s return
Fate of Gaspar’s ship
entries.name: Gaspar Corte-Real’s second voyage
entries.region: North Atlantic and eastern North America

entries.note: Góis dates the Lisbon departure and the biography records an August rendezvous, but the rendezvous site and the course of Miguel’s ship are unresolved.
remainingQuestions: Identification of the meeting place and when surviving ships returned
entries.name: Miguel Corte-Real’s search
entries.region: North Atlantic and eastern North America

entries.note: The second expedition’s Harwich departure, Greenland approach and Frobisher Bay mining phase have dated observations.
remainingQuestions: Ship-by-ship homeward route and precise locations of the three captures
entries.name: Frobisher’s second Arctic voyage

entries.note: The outward fleet and an English return sighting are represented. Work at the camp retains month precision and the fleet’s scattered movements require ship-by-ship study.
remainingQuestions: Individual Hudson Strait excursions and dated mining-camp arrival and departure
entries.name: Frobisher’s third Arctic voyage

entries.note: Red Bay documents recurring whaling and ship losses. The cautiously identified San Juan wreck is a site with year-level chronology and does not establish a dated voyage track.
remainingQuestions: Ship-specific log dates and the identity of the Red Bay wreck
entries.name: Basque whaling and the reported loss of the San Juan

entries.note: The first voyage now includes Cumberland Sound and the homeward passage.
remainingQuestions: Local day positions in Cumberland Sound
entries.name: Davis’s first Northwest Passage voyage

entries.note: The main voyage has five dated anchors. The separate Sunshine, North Star and Mermaid movements have only selected context here.
remainingQuestions: Independent courses of the other three vessels after separating
entries.name: Davis’s second Northwest Passage voyage

entries.note: The leader’s small exploration vessel is documented separately from the fishing barks.
remainingQuestions: Exact separation position and day-dated courses of the independent fishing barks
entries.name: Davis’s third Northwest Passage voyage

entries.note: The first Discovery survey now has independent outward, Hudson Strait and return anchors.
remainingQuestions: Exact dates and modern positions of some Southampton Island survey legs
entries.name: Bylot and Baffin’s first Discovery voyage

entries.note: The outward and return itinerary now includes dated Jones and Lancaster Sound approaches and the Dover arrival.
remainingQuestions: Modern identification of Hall’s Cockin Sound and finer nearshore survey positions
entries.name: Bylot and Baffin’s second Discovery voyage
Orellana, Carvajal and the Amazon expeditions
entries.note: A previously absent family gains lower-Amazon confluence observations, ocean exit and larger-vessel return. The smaller brigantine’s earlier arrival is a separate point. Upper-river and second-expedition activity remain at supported coarse precision.
remainingQuestions: Reconcile early Coca/Napo camps and river identifications before drawing a route from the December 1541 separation.
The 26 August numeric ocean-exit date conflicts with the Saint Louis feast label.
Resolve the offshore brigantine separation location, Paria passage dates, second-expedition delta channels and survivor routes.

entries.name: Champlain’s Great Lakes campaign and return
entries.region: St. Lawrence, Great Lakes and Atlantic
entries.note: The previously unmapped 1615–16 phase now carries Champlain’s party through Wendat country and its documented return to France. Regional pins and gaps separate it from the earlier Le Caron party, the detached interpreter, and unsettled war/winter sites.
remainingQuestions: Resolve competing archaeological identifications of Otouacha, Carhagouha, Cahiagué and the attacked Haudenosaunee fort before adding tighter geometry.
Date and locate the separate Le Caron and interpreter parties, additional winter visits, and Champlain’s other voyages including 1603, Acadian surveys and 1613.

entries.name: Chirikov’s St. Paul and detached boats
entries.note: Previously absent family gains seven ship anchors and separate boat-dispatch activities.
remainingQuestions: Reconcile September 9/10 Adak and September 21/22 Agattu against the original log; selected dates follow journal headings.
Boat landing sites and fate remain unresolved.
Recover corrected daily ocean fixes before enabling interpolation.

entries.name: Matonabbee and Hearne’s Coppermine journey
entries.note: Previously absent family gains secure endpoints, river-mouth survey and regionally located Great Slave Lake arrival.
remainingQuestions: Intermediate lake identifications require further geographic and Indigenous place-name research.
Earlier attempts and separate family movements are not mapped.

entries.name: Rae’s survey and Inuit testimony
entries.note: Year-level evidence gains separate land and boat routes and Mistegan’s independent reconnaissance.
remainingQuestions: Extract the 1853 boats and Quoich River exploration from the full correspondence.
Reconcile historical longitude errors without substituting later memorial coordinates.
Mistegan’s exact endpoint remains unlocated.

entries.name: Bougainville, Boudeuse and Étoile
entries.note: Previously absent family. Thirteen Boudeuse anchors now cover the outward Atlantic, American ports, Pacific and return; Étoile’s separate homeward movement is coarse activity.
remainingQuestions: Extract Étoile’s independent outward and return logs and Jeanne Baret/Commerson shore-party chronology.
Recover Strait of Magellan, Tuamotu, Samoa, Vanuatu, Louisiade and New Guinea intermediate positions before drawing these gaps.
Resolve the printed ship-calendar adjustment against civil dates before declaring universal exact event dates.

entries.name: Dampier’s American and Pacific voyages
entries.note: Previously absent family. Nine Cygnet anchors cover the major 1686–1688 trans-Pacific and Asian/Australian phase.
remainingQuestions: Extract the 1679–1682 Caribbean/Darién phase, Bachelor’s Delight 1683–1685, the Nicobar canoe party and later voyages as independent identities.
Verify precise Guam, Mindanao and northwest Australia anchorages without treating obsolete latitude values as modern exact locations.

entries.name: Bellingshausen and Lazarev
entries.note: The second Antarctic season is added using the BAS published dataset; approximate reconstructed positions and calendar uncertainty are explicit.
remainingQuestions: Check each selected dataset coordinate against the original journal because interpolated coordinates are not individually flagged.
Extract the first-season continuation and separate Mirny/Vostok returns after 17 March 1820.
Reconcile Old Style, ship day and the February 1821 date-line correction; do not settle sighting priority from an anniversary timeline.

entries.name: Wilkes · United States Exploring Expedition
entries.note: Existing three-anchor expedition track remains very partial. No new merged fleet route is proposed in this bounded pass.
remainingQuestions: Extract Vincennes, Peacock, Porpoise and Flying Fish independently from Wilkes’s five-volume Narrative; Columbia-bar travel must not automatically continue the Antarctic ship.
Add 1839 South American/Antarctic sorties, 1840 Fiji survey, Hawaiian work, Peacock wreck and separate Columbia/Sacramento overland parties only after party-specific chronology is established.

entries.name: Cavendish · first and second expeditions
entries.note: Significant absent family identified, held behind source-ready Bougainville, Dampier and Bellingshausen in this bounded pass.
remainingQuestions: Extract Pretty’s narrative in Hakluyt for the 1586–1588 voyage and separate the 1591–1593 ships/parties. No day-dated anchors have been asserted from biographical summaries.

entries.name: Schouten and Le Maire, Cape Horn and the global return
entries.region: Atlantic, Patagonia, South Pacific and East Indies
remainingQuestions: Reconcile the Tuamotu island names and New Guinea stages against Le Maire’s independent journal and scanned originals before assigning additional modern coordinates.
Resolve the source’s corrupt December death-day text for Jacob Le Maire; do not infer a death position from the return route.
Determine the exact Mauritius anchorage and Zeeland arrival harbour. The account gives only island/province-level places.
Keep the recorded Jacatra one-day discrepancy and the source calendar convention visible when comparing other chronologies.
entries.note: Twenty selected anchors distinguish the Eendracht voyage from the return aboard Amsterdam. Modern named-place locations replace demonstrably inaccurate southern latitudes. No daily track or globally complete voyage inventory is claimed.

entries.name: Slocum and Spray, with American and global stages
entries.region: North and South America, Pacific, Australia, Indian Ocean and Atlantic
remainingQuestions: Reconcile the Gibraltar departure weekday/date conflict and the Ascension 26/27 April arrival contradiction with another edition or Slocum’s surviving journal.
Identify the unnamed Uruguay stranding beach of 11 December 1895 and the exact temporary Fuegian shelters without invented geographic precision.
Resolve the undated Marquesas sighting and the printed Nukahiva/southernmost-island discrepancy.
Complete the early New England/Nova Scotia visits, Tasmania circuit, local reef navigation, Simons Bay shelter and undated Cape Town arrival from additional date evidence.
entries.note: Selected dated anchors span the full circumnavigation and final homecoming. Gaps represent absent track evidence, not an assertion that the voyage jumped directly between ports. Newport return and Fairhaven homecoming remain distinct; the local river excursion passenger is disclosed.

sources.authors: Hernando de Alarcón; Richard Hakluyt (translator); Albert B. Elsasser (editor)
sources.title: Explorations of Hernando Alarcon in the Lower Colorado River Region, 1540
sources.venue: Journal of California and Great Basin Anthropology 1(1), pp. 8–37; UC Merced eScholarship
sources.access: Reprints and annotates Alarcón’s letter through Ramusio and Hakluyt. The Spanish original and promised full report are lost. Printed pages 10–11 and 28–31 give distinct sea and boat phases; modern identification of the upstream limit remains uncertain.

sources.title: Descubrimiento del río de las Amazonas

sources.authors: Samuel de Champlain; Charles Pomeroy Otis (translator); Edmund F. Slafter (editor)
sources.title: Voyages of Samuel de Champlain, volume III: 1611–1618
sources.venue: Prince Society, Boston / Canadian Institute for Historical Microreproductions / Internet Archive
sources.access: Participant narrative with explicit editorial annotations. Printed pp. 111–144 and 184–187 support the selected 1615–16 inland and return observations. The editor’s inferred dates and archaeological identifications are distinguished from Champlain’s words.

sources.title: Champlain Committee: Champlain’s Legacy
sources.access: Institutional historical interpretation locates Cahiagué in Wendat country near present Orillia; it does not establish an exact archaeological site for every journal observation.

sources.authors: Alexei Chirikov and expedition officers; Frank A. Golder (editor); Ellsworth P. Bertholf (reconstruction)
sources.title: Bering’s Voyages, volume I: The Log Books and Official Reports
sources.venue: American Geographical Society / Distributed Proofreaders Canada

sources.title: A Journey from Prince of Wales’s Fort in Hudson’s Bay to the Northern Ocean
sources.access: Scholarly edition of the 1795 narrative. Tyrrell’s place identifications are distinguished from Hearne’s testimony.

sources.title: Rae, John (1813–93)

sources.access: Institutional biography, revised 2020; explicit March 31 departure and expedition context.

sources.title: Report to the Hudson’s Bay Company, York Factory, 1 September 1854
sources.venue: House of Commons sessional papers 1854–55, vol. 35, no. 1898, pp. 835–844 / Great Unsolved Mysteries in Canadian History

sources.title: Documentary extracts from journals and logbooks relating to the circum-Antarctic expeditions of Cook (1772–75) and Bellingshausen (1819–21), Version 1.0

sources.access: Open Government Licence v3.0. Journal-derived observational dataset; occasional missing positions are interpolated without a per-row flag. Dates were advanced 12 days from Old Style. Date-line correction is separately noted at 17 February 1821.

sources.title: The Southern Ocean marine ice record of the early historical, circum-Antarctic voyages of Cook and Bellingshausen

sources.title: A Voyage Round the World

sources.access: Public-domain primary narrative. Dates retain the English account convention. Chapter XIV, pp. 376–378 discusses the difference between ship and local calendar days.
